review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Japanese juvenile and Northwestern Pacific adult tagging support broad thermal and vertical habitat context, but neither establishes a universal West Coast catch curve or bathymetric preference.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for pacific bluefin tuna.
factors.value_notes: Archival tags on young Pacific bluefin tuna reported preference for 14-20 °C water. A 2025 Northwestern Pacific study tagged three adult spawning fish and recorded temperatures from 16-32 °C during vertical movements, with substantial individual and day/night variation. This supports the configured 15-22 °C / 17-20 °C interval as broad context, but juvenile and adult data, Japanese/Northwestern Pacific locations, and spawning-season behavior are not a validated West Coast catch-response curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for pacific bluefin tuna.
factors.value_notes: Pacific bluefin are highly migratory pelagic tuna. Tagging records vertical movements from the surface to hundreds of metres and, in adult spawning fish, deep dives exceeding 1,000 m. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not tuna vertical depth; the configured 0-200 m seabed interval is only a weak shelf/offshore context proxy, not a preferred bottom-depth band.
